findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_entrypoints.py: `def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:`; `if name not in ENTRYPOINTS: raise EntrypointError(...)`; `raise EntrypointError(f"entrypoint {name!r} requires its payload from the private boundary; " "it must not fetch or synthesise one itself")`. The registered command is `("python", CONTAINER_ENTRYPOINT_PATH, name)` in `_spec`, but `main` contains no call to `ENTRYPOINTS[name].function`.
findings.reproduction: Invoke the committed container command for any role, for example `python /app/src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_entrypoints.py stage-p`. `main()` accepts the registered name and then raises EntrypointError without invoking `run_stage_p` or any other registered callable.
findings.residual_limitation: A dispatch fix would bind the command to a callable, but would not by itself prove that Azure launched the intended image or supplied the intended payload.
findings.title: The deployed container command never dispatches a registered entrypoint

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_entrypoints.py: `class RoleConfig` contains `image_digest: str` and `config_digest: str` but no schema digest; `assert_config_registered` validates `config.config_digest` only with `if not _SHA256.match(config.config_digest or "")`; `ROLE_SCHEMAS` stores only schema ID strings. infra/azure/parser_v3_v2_boundary/modules/workload.bicep: the container environment includes `JSPACE_SCHEMA_IDS` and `JSPACE_IMAGE_DIGEST`, but no schema-registry digest or configuration digest. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_schemas.py: `SCHEMA_DIGESTS` and `REGISTRY_DIGEST` are computed, but `assert_registry_matches` is only defined and is not invoked in the supplied production path.
findings.reproduction: Replace the schema document or role/configuration JSON while retaining the same schema ID and role names. The entrypoint configuration checks the ID and only checks that `config_digest` has SHA-256 syntax; the workload template passes schema IDs, not a bound schema digest, and no production call compares the registry to a pre-bound digest.
findings.residual_limitation: Digest binding would establish content identity for the supplied artifacts, but would not prove that Azure actually deployed the recorded digest without deployment read-back evidence.
findings.title: Schema and configuration content are not runtime-bound by digest

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_entrypoints.py: `expected_identity = ROLE_IDENTITY_NAMES.get(config.role)` and `if config.uami_name != expected_identity`; `if not _GUID.match(config.uami_client_id or "")`; `supplied = environment.get("AZURE_CLIENT_ID")`; `if supplied != config.uami_client_id`. The code never verifies a mapping from the registered `uami_name` to the supplied client ID or to an Azure identity object.
findings.reproduction: Construct a `RoleConfig` for a registered role with its expected `uami_name` and any syntactically valid GUID as `uami_client_id`, then provide the same GUID as `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`. The identity assertions pass even though the GUID is not bound in the supplied material to that role's managed identity.
findings.residual_limitation: A name-to-client-ID binding would still not prove that the Azure workload token at runtime corresponds to that identity without a runtime canary or control-plane read-back.
findings.title: Managed identity is not bound to the registered identity name

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_entrypoints.py: `FORBIDDEN_CREDENTIAL_MARKERS` is a fixed tuple of marker strings; `hits = sorted({key for key in environment for marker in FORBIDDEN_CREDENTIAL_MARKERS if marker in key.casefold()})`; the only separate fallback check is `environment.get("AZURE_USE_AMBIENT_CREDENTIAL", "").strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes"}`.
findings.reproduction: Call `assert_no_ambient_credentials` with an environment containing `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` plus a differently named credential such as `FOO_TOKEN=secret` or `MY_STORAGE_AUTH=secret`. Neither key contains any listed marker and the function returns without refusal.
findings.residual_limitation: Rejecting all unapproved environment variables or using an explicit allowlist would still not detect credentials injected through files, process metadata, or platform token endpoints.
findings.title: Ambient-credential refusal is an incomplete denylist

findings.evidence: infra/azure/parser_v3_v2_boundary/modules/observability.bicep: `resource workspace 'Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces@2023-09-01'`; `publicNetworkAccessForIngestion: 'Enabled'`; `publicNetworkAccessForQuery: 'Enabled'`. The same module sends firewall and registry evidence to `workspace.id` through diagnostic settings.
findings.reproduction: Deploy the committed observability module and inspect the workspace properties: both ingestion and query public-network settings are explicitly Enabled, while the module configures private-boundary firewall and registry events to that workspace.
findings.residual_limitation: Disabling public access would not by itself prove that logs contain no private material or that every control-plane access path is private.
findings.title: The observability workspace has public network access enabled

findings.evidence: infra/azure/parser_v3_v2_boundary/modules/network.bicep: `targetFqdns: [ 'mcr.microsoft.com' '*.data.mcr.microsoft.com' resourceManagerHost 'login.microsoft.com' loginHost '*.blob.${storageSuffix}' 'packages.microsoft.com' 'acs-mirror.azureedge.net' ]`. These are literal environment/service hostnames in the firewall allowlist.
findings.reproduction: Search the committed Bicep files for literal hostnames. The listed URLs remain in the deployed firewall policy independently of `environment()` and therefore are not portable or content-bound to the selected Azure environment.
findings.residual_limitation: Deriving endpoints from the environment would not establish that the resulting allowlist is sufficient or least-privilege for the platform.
findings.title: IaC contains hardcoded cloud environment URLs

findings.evidence: tests/test_parser_v3_v2_boundary_iac.py: `_read_text(path)` returns the complete file text; `test_the_runtime_registry_is_private` asserts `"publicNetworkAccess: 'Disabled'" in text` and `"networkRuleBypassOptions: 'None'" in text`; `test_the_environment_has_no_public_ingress` asserts `"internal: true" in text`; `test_the_custom_write_role_cannot_delete` asserts `"blobs/delete" not in text`. These checks use raw text rather than a parsed Bicep declaration or compiled template. The file itself documents that several controls are text-level checks.
findings.reproduction: Move a required positive declaration into a comment while removing the actual declaration, or place a forbidden token in a comment. The positive substring assertions still pass in the first case, and negative substring assertions fail or can be defeated by changing the tested text representation rather than the resource semantics.
findings.residual_limitation: Parsing or compiling the template would still not prove Azure's deployed resource properties without control-plane read-back.
findings.title: Source-text security tests can be satisfied by comments

report.summary: The registry and entrypoint tables are substantially closed, but the deployed binding is not. The container command reaches main(), which validates a name and then unconditionally raises instead of dispatching the registered callable. Runtime configuration does not bind schema or config content by digest, identity client IDs are only checked for GUID shape and equality to caller-supplied configuration, ambient-credential detection is an incomplete name-marker denylist, and the observability workspace has public ingestion and query enabled. The IaC also hardcodes cloud environment URLs and relies on comment-vulnerable text-substring tests.
unverifiable_without_private_material: Whether Azure actually deployed the image, configuration, schema registry, and role matrix contents represented by the committed files.
Whether the dependency lock is the closure Azure installs.
Whether the deployed managed identity tokens correspond to the role identities.
Whether runtime canaries observed the claimed network, lane, and import-isolation refusals.
Whether any tests outside the supplied material were weakened, removed, skipped, or xfailed.
